confirmed.title: One non-finite sample (NaN or Inf) deafens the detector for the rest of the session
confirmed.demonstration: Tests/TunkCoreTests/AuditDetectorProbeTests.swift. testANaNSampleDoesNotDeafenTheDetectorForever: same synthetic stream, one sample's z set to .nan 376.8 ms in, clean double-tap 1.1 s later. Control run: 1 trigger, 2 onsets. Poisoned run: 0 triggers, 0 onsets. testAnInfiniteSampleDoesNotDeafenTheDetectorForever: x = .infinity, 0 triggers vs 1. testANaNSampleAfterAGestureDoesNotDeafenTheNext: gesture, NaN, gesture 2.5 s later fires 1 of 2, and after the stream detector.envelope and detector.noiseFloor both read nan. Trace: Detector.swift:206 hands Double(sample.x) to the chain; OnePoleHighPass.process (DSP.swift:40) does y = c*(prevOut + x - prevIn), so after one NaN prevIn and prevOut are NaN and every later output is NaN; NoiseFloorTracker.update then makes the floor NaN; envelope >= threshold is false forever, so the detector never declares an onset again until reset(). The gap-reset path (Detector.swift:196) covers dropped samples but not bad values. AccelReader.read (Sources/TunkFormat/Session.swift:341) builds Float(bitPattern:) with no finiteness check, so a corrupted recording replays as silent zero detections rather than an error.
confirmed.fix: In TapDetector.ingest(sample:) before the chain call at Detector.swift:206: `guard sample.x.isFinite, sample.y.isFinite, sample.z.isFinite else { dropSignalState(); lastSampleNs = sample.tNs; return nil }` (treat a bad value like a dropout). No clock, no new state.

confirmed.title: Watchdog closes the stderr read end, so a Shortcut that outlives it is killed by SIGPIPE on its next stderr write (the contract says it is left running)
confirmed.demonstration: Tests/TunkCoreTests/AuditEmitTests.swift, AuditSpawnerWatchdogTests.testChildThatOutlivesTheWatchdogIsKilledOnItsNextStderrWrite (fails as intended). Executable: `( echo $$ > pid; sleep 0.6; echo 'still going' >&2; touch done; exit 0 ); echo $? > status`, watchdog 0.2 s. Output: `AUDIT child pid 68522 after watchdog: ps -> [] inner exit status [141]`, `AUDIT marker exists: false`. 141 = 128+SIGPIPE; the line after the stderr write never ran. Control test testSameChildFinishesWhenNoWatchdogClosesThePipe (watchdog 0) passes: marker created, outcome succeeded. The real CLI behaves the same: `/usr/bin/shortcuts run zzz 2>&1 >/dev/null | true` -> PIPESTATUS[0]=141, versus exit 1 with stderr to a file. Path: once.onFire (line 114-116) runs on the watchdog path and closes errPipe.fileHandleForReading; the child's next write(2) to fd 2 has no reader. Docstring at line 51 and testWatchdogSurfacesAShortcutThatNeverFinishes both assert the process is deliberately not killed.
confirmed.fix: On the watchdog path do not close the read end. Replace the readabilityHandler with a discard reader (read availableData, drop it) so the child never sees EPIPE, and close the handle in terminationHandler / the run() failure path only. Cost is one read fd per hung child until it exits; testFileDescriptorsAfterHungSpawns measured 4 -> 4 -> 4 fds across 30 hung spawns with the current code, so the leak that motivated the close is gone either way while the child is reaped.

confirmed.title: Off-means-off guard is an unsynchronized cross-thread read: TSan reports a data race on wantsRunning
confirmed.demonstration: Built with `swift build --scratch-path .build-audit-tsan --sanitize=thread` and ran `TSAN_OPTIONS=halt_on_error=0 ./.build-audit-tsan/debug/tunk --reacquire-probe 5`. Output: `WARNING: ThreadSanitizer: data race — Write of size 1 by main thread: #0 Engine.setEnabled(_:) Engine.swift:312 ... Previous read of size 1 by thread T2 (GCD worker): #0 Engine.feed(sample:) Engine.swift:492 ... #3 AccelSource.handle(event:) AccelSource.swift:233 ... __IOHIDEventSystemClientQueueCallback. SUMMARY: ThreadSanitizer: data race Engine.swift:312 in Engine.setEnabled(_:)`. The probe's own counters still print CLEAN/ALIVE/SETTLED because they only count off-main @Published writes. RESUME records `TSan clean across three 20-cycle runs` and then, later in the same round, the `guard wantsRunning` fix in feed(sample:); the race is the fix itself (main writes `wantsRunning` at :312 with no lock, the accel queue reads it at :492 with no lock), and no TSan run is recorded after it landed.
confirmed.fix: Make the guard a lock-protected flag: in feed(sample:) take detectorLock first and check the flag under it; write the flag under detectorLock in start() (after the monitor is installed) and in stopSensors(). That also fixes finding 3 (see below), since stopSensors() is the one path every gate-removal shares.
